title: RSA was invented twice. A 22 year old at British intelligence found it first, in 1973.
description:
A 22 year old at British intelligence found it first, in 1973. The public inventors, Rivest, Shamir and Adleman, published in 1977.

Joined GCHQ's CESG in September. His surviving note is dated 20 November.

Nick Patterson told him about James Ellis's "non-secret encryption". Ellis had the concept but no way to make it work.

The work stayed classified for 24 years. Cocks spoke about it publicly on 18 December 1997.

The internet's lock existed before the internet needed one.

Sources:
- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clifford_Cocks (read): established that Cocks joined GCHQ's CESG in September 1973, aged about 22, that Nick Patterson told him of James Ellis's non-secret encryption idea (published internally in 1969 but never implemented), that his surviving note is dated 20 November 1973, that he revealed the work in a public talk on 18 December 1997, and that Rivest, Shamir and Adleman independently published RSA in 1977.
- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Public-key_cryptography (read): established that Ellis conceived non-secret encryption in 1970, Cocks implemented the RSA equivalent in 1973, Williamson found the Diffie-Hellman equivalent in 1974, that all of it stayed secret until the British government declassified it in 1997, and that Diffie and Hellman published in 1976.
